title: Sharp Bounds on Trajectory Shapley Credit under Shared Counterfactual Coupling
banked_reason: Fresh full-packet review accepted the sound repaired shared-SCM construction, but the D0.5 score ceiling is 7.3, below the 7.5 field threshold.
gap_reasons: The D0.5 ceiling is 7.3, which caps the assignable tier at subfield (field needs 7.5), so acceptance is arithmetically impossible.
Generic row gluing is already in Lally et al., so novelty is confined to shared sequential optimization and compression.
proof_attempt_summary: The final atomic D0 repair made factual and coalition policy coins jointly independent, synchronized mutual transition-row CI, narrowed the published comparison to transition components, restored ambient metadata, and repaired malformed TeX; fresh review accepted all 63 changes and replay passed. Ten reviewed proof bodies persist, but dependency invalidation leaves the compiler, confidence-fiber, sparse-width, active-chain, and two supporting results marked partial/to-prove. The topic is banked below the field floor because its assessed ceiling is 7.3 rather than the required 7.5, not because the repaired model is unsound.
tldr: Trajectory-conditioned Shapley credit is not point identified by a Markov transition kernel once counterfactual independence across action rows is removed. Each coordinate is the attained interval obtained by optimizing one posterior response-row kernel shared across all coalition worlds. In the complete two-step binary family \(\mathfrak G_{\varepsilon}\), that interval is \([-\varepsilon,\varepsilon/2]\), strictly inside the coalitionwise interval \([-(1+\varepsilon)/2,1/2]\) on an open neighborhood. Exact beta-integral compression replaces the \(2^H\) coalition sum by \(H\) Markov polynomial evaluations, and an explicit reward-range affine lift produces two nonnegative objectives without duplicating row choices. The central open question is a rational constrained-width compiler whose legal sum-before-max order and backpointers retain one shared optimizer and return a compatible endpoint SCM. A simultaneous multinomial confidence fiber covers every coordinate interval on one event, with endpoint error controlled by the smallest factual transition probability.
gap: Existing trajectory credit selects counterfactual independence, generic Layer-3 bounds do not exploit Markov structure, and compatible-MDP row bounds do not solve a signed Shapley objective sharing one SCM across coalitions. Existing exact Shapley and marginal-MAP algorithms separately address coalition redundancy or mixed operators, but not their posterior shared-coupling composition.
fill: The project supplies attained shared-SCM intervals and witnesses, a fully specified binary strict-gap family with explicit endpoint assignments and open-neighborhood persistence, exact polynomial Shapley compression, a signed-to-nonnegative affine lift, a width-parameterized shared-optimizer compiler question, and whole-set multinomial confidence-fiber inference with a local positivity modulus.
